summary: SplunkAOCallback already produces one workflow, tool, and model operation per demo turn; preserve it as the sole producer.

The callback serializes raw inputs and outputs. The synthetic examples are approved for this local fixture, but run_demo accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied question; that content boundary is not enforced before callback capture.
ingestion_hook captures completed traces in memory and does not establish live Splunk delivery.

evidence.finding: Pinned Splunk AO LangChain integration with a local deterministic model
run_demo passes an arbitrary question into the callback-covered chain and terminates the logger in finally
This fixture is a CLI runnable, not an HTTP service
Makefile runs the local Python application and focused tests
The local captured batch includes synthetic content and arbitrary caller text in raw callback input/output fields

signal_flow.component_flow_map: run_demo question [GAP: Splunk AO callback content boundary] -> SplunkAOCallback [SOURCE-COVERED] -> ingestion_hook [SOURCE-COVERED]

genai_readiness.required_signals: Preserve one workflow, tool, and model node while allowing only approved synthetic question content to enter callback raw input/output fields.
genai_readiness.owner: Application-owned run_demo input boundary in app.py
genai_readiness.acceptance_criteria: A synthetic demo question still creates one nested callback trace; an unapproved arbitrary question is rejected before any callback-covered operation starts.
genai_readiness.impact: Without an enforced boundary, production-like caller text can be captured as raw trace content.

findings.title: Enforce the callback content boundary
findings.gap: run_demo accepts arbitrary caller questions even though SplunkAOCallback records raw chain and model input content.
findings.impact: Unapproved question text can enter the captured trace batch and, with a production exporter, leave the process.
findings.product_outcome: Only explicitly approved synthetic demo questions enter callback-captured raw fields while the existing trace tree remains intact.
findings.required_fix: Use an explicit allowlist of approved synthetic demo questions or a source-verified raw-capture suppression control before invoking the callback-covered chain; preserve SplunkAOCallback as the only chain, model, and tool span producer.
acceptance_criteria: An approved synthetic question produces exactly one support_agent workflow with one lookup_weather tool and one DemoLocalLLM model child.
An arbitrary unapproved question is rejected before callback capture; no raw prompt, tool argument, or model output escapes through a second instrumentation path.
constraints: Do not patch splunk-ao or install a second LangChain callback, decorator, or application-owned OTel span around the same operations.
Do not mistake companion redacted fields for removal of the raw callback input/output fields.

expected_telemetry.name: splunk-ao.callback.content-boundary
expected_telemetry.product_view: Safe callback-owned Agent Observability trace content

follow_up_actions: Inspect the in-memory callback batch and verify both the synthetic content boundary and duplicate-free tree.

environments.prerequisites: Install pinned dependencies before isolated offline execution; the application itself uses FakeListLLM and ingestion_hook and needs no provider, Splunk credential, or network.

scenarios.trigger: Call run_demo with an approved synthetic question, then with an unapproved arbitrary question
scenarios.expected_signals: One callback-owned workflow/tool/model tree for synthetic content; no callback-captured trace for unapproved content
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: The local captured batch contains exactly one support_agent workflow with one lookup_weather and one DemoLocalLLM child, and unapproved content is rejected before chain.invoke.

anti_patterns: Do not add duplicate @log decorators or OTel spans around callback-owned operations.
Do not claim ingestion_hook proves live Splunk delivery.
recommendation: Select OTEL-001 and run $otel-instrument to enforce the callback content boundary, then verify the local captured tree.
